newsitem.title: ABU DHABI: UAE halts deals with Italian arms firms after tussle.
newsitem.headline: UAE halts deals with Italian arms firms after tussle.

text.p: The UAE said on Tuesday it would not deal with any Italian arms firms until a 1994 dispute with Italy's BPD Difesa e Spazio (Fiat Avio Group) over a rocket launching system was resolved.

Colonel Obeid al-Kitbi, the United Arab Emirates deputy director general of arms procurements, told a news conference at the Gulf Arab states' IDEX arms show that all efforts to resolve the "technical problem" with BPD had failed so far.
"The UAE armed forces...announces that there is a problem between them and BPD related to technical problems that appeared in the rocket launching system supplied by them in 1984," he said.

"And all efforts failed to convince the Italian company to resolve this problem in spite of the intervention by the Italian government in this matter which is liable to jeopardise our business relationship with Italian companies until we reach a suitable and acceptable solution to this problem," Kitbi said.
"We found the trust is not really there so far to have any further deals with any other (Italian) companies until we get this problem resolved," Kitbi said.
He said this decision only applied to UAE military contracts, not to civilian deals.
"This is bad news for the rest of us," said an Italian arms industry source attending the Abu Dhabi international arms show.
The UAE withdrew the Italian-made rapid launcher rocket system from military use in 1996 due to a recurring technical malfunction.

The 24 multiple launchers and thousands of surface-to- surface rockets, with a 30-km (19 miles) range, were bought in the 1980s for $280 million, officials said. The problem did not appear until 1994.

The announcement came one day after the UAE said the Eurofighter re-entered a contest to sell Abu Dhabi up to 80 warplanes, competing with original favourites Lockheed Martin and France's Dassault in the $6 billion race.

Italian company Alenia Spa, a unit of state-controlled engineering group Finmeccanica, is one of the partners in the Eurofighter programme. The others are British Aerospace, Germany's Daimler-Benz Aerospace (DASA) and Spain's CASA.

Kitbi said that the UAE was still in the early stages of studying the programme but added that at this point there was no link between Tuesday's the decision and Eurofighter's bid to win the aircraft contract.
